hook: Your platform isn't 'Azure with AI bolted on.' If agents are first-class actors, your identity, orchestration, and observability models have to change with them.
angle: Use Microsoft's 'designing agent-first platforms' argument, plus the Foundry model-choice and agent-shipping announcements, to frame the platform decisions that actually matter once agents do the work — and why 'we'll swap the model later' is an architecture promise, not a strategy.

hook: MCP is quietly becoming the connective tissue between agents — and its trust model is a structural risk, not a bug.
angle: Take the Ars Technica MCP vulnerability report and turn it into an architect's checklist: agent identity, egress control, prompt provenance, and blast-radius limits for any multi-agent system touching regulated data. Pair it with GitHub's open-source security agent as the 'inspectable automation' counterexample.

hook: You can't benchmark AI code review on vibes. Now there's a production-aligned, open benchmark.
angle: ReviewBench plus Copilot Plugins show AI review and standardized agentic artifacts are becoming measurable, governable pipeline stages. Connect that to why regulated change-control needs evidence and version control, not vendor promises.

hook: Data residency isn't a cloud-exit story. GA of SQL Server on Azure Local means you can modernize where the data already lives.
angle: For healthcare and finance clients, frame SQL Server on Azure Local plus FabCon's governed-data messaging as a modernization path that respects residency and sovereignty constraints without a forced lift-and-shift. Compliance impact is a consideration, not a recommendation.

hook: Resilience isn't the diagram you approved last year. It's a property you maintain — and auditors increasingly ask you to prove it.
angle: Use 'Your architecture diagram is not your resilience' to shift the conversation from static DR artifacts to measured, continuously verified recovery objectives, with an eye on audit and business-continuity evidence in regulated environments.
